paper.title_en: From Macroscopic Quantum Tunneling to Circuit QED: Coherence and Dissipation in 3D Transmon Qubits
paper.abstract_en: Superconducting quantum circuits are a leading platform for quantum-information processing, but their development requires expertise spanning device design, microfabrication, cryogenic operation, microwave control, and quantum characterization. In this work, we report the realization of a flux-tunable superconducting transmon platform and present an integrated workflow encompassing design, fabrication, measurement, and numerical modeling. The device consists of an $Al/AlO_x/Al$ transmon coupled to a three-dimensional microwave cavity operating in the circuit quantum electrodynamics (cQED) dispersive regime. Two-tone spectroscopy reveals a fundamental transition frequency of $\omega _{01}=5.0122~\textrm{GHz}$ and an anharmonicity of $\alpha /2\pi =-202.4~\textrm{MHz}$, corresponding to $E_J/E_C \approx 82.9$. Flux spectroscopy yields a cavity-qubit coupling strength of $g/2\pi = 260~\textrm{MHz}$, while the cavity linewidth gives a loaded quality factor of $Q_L=6127$ and a Purcell limit of $T_1^{\textrm{Purcell}}\approx 82~\mu \textrm{s}$. Time-domain measurements yield coherence times of $T_1 = 17.4~\mu \textrm{s}$ and $T_2^* = 5.8~\mu \textrm{s}$. To investigate coherence and dissipation in the device, the experimental observations are analyzed within a Lindblad master-equation framework describing cavity photon loss and thermal excitation, qubit energy relaxation, and pure dephasing processes. Using a set of experimentally extracted parameters, the model reproduces the measured spectroscopic and time-domain observables, providing a quantitative description of the open-system dynamics of the transmon-cavity platform. The analysis shows that the measured coherence is primarily limited by pure dephasing and energy-relaxation processes, whereas thermal excitation plays a minor role under the experimental conditions. Inspired by the broader framework of quantum dissipation in macroscopic quantum systems pioneered by Caldeira and collaborators, this approach enables a quantitative analysis of relaxation and dephasing processes in superconducting quantum circuits. Beyond the characterization of a single device, the present work demonstrates the establishment of the expertise, infrastructure, and experimental workflow required for the design, fabrication, measurement, and modeling of superconducting quantum circuits, contributing to the development of quantum technologies in Brazil and related applications.
